answer: An agent economy can anchor trust to a refundable stake: before an agent may trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if it cheats. One identity, one stake, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake separately and the cost grows linearly, while honest agents pay nothing beyond the lockup. Like a comet, a flood of fresh identities burns bright but briefly; at its nadir the attack collapses, because each new sock puppet costs real money while reputation earned over time makes old identities far more valuable than new ones.
